Subject: Exploring Dedicated — credits / bridge months / commit options

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers on short-context workflows. We're ready to start a formal evaluation of Dedicated for our high-throughput scoring pipelines. Two items procurement asked me to clarify before we put anything on paper:

1) Conversion credits: if we move from hosted to Dedicated, what are the mechanics and timing for converting our hosted usage into committed dollars? Can credits be phased across multiple months?
2) Commit offsets and bridge months: we'd like to avoid billing cliffs between the end of hosted credits and the Dedicated reservation kicking in. Is there a standard 'bridge month' approach or a prorated ramp you recommend?
3) GPU pool sizing & throughput: rough guidance on minimum pool sizing for sustained 10k tokens/sec across ~30 concurrent streams (latency target ~150–200ms tail) would be helpful to include in the SOW.

Attached our procurement tracker (procurement@nimbus.ai) with target procurement dates. Can you loop in the appropriate folks on your side?

Cheers,
Jake

Nimbus Analytics

Jake — great to hear, and thanks for the clear list. Looping in Aditya (inference sizing) and Karthik (commercials). High level answers below; I'll follow up with a short proposal PDF.

1) Conversion credits: we typically convert eligible hosted spend into a time-phased credit that applies against the first 6–12 months of a Dedicated commit. Credits can be front-loaded (larger in month 1–3) or smoothed — we can structure either.

2) Bridge months: two standard options — a) a one or two month complimentary bridge where hosted continues and Dedicated billing begins after the bridge, or b) prorated overlap where we apply credits to a portion of the first Dedicated invoice to avoid a cliff. For larger deals we also offer a 'safety-net' credit that shields uptime SLO breaches during the first 30 days.

3) GPU pool sizing & throughput: Aditya, can you provide a conservative GPU pool and recommended guardrails for Jake's 10k tokens/sec target? Also note quantization and batching profiles will materially affect footprint.

I attached an initial offer doc for your review.

— Evelyn

Jake — quick sizing note from infra: assuming model family similar to the demo (2B–6B variants) and a mix of short (<=256 tokens) and occasional long (<=1024 tokens) contexts, the safe starting point for 10k tokens/sec sustained is:

- 8 x A40-equivalent GPUs in a single pool (with autoscale headroom to +25%);
- Continuous batching with a target batch latency window of 30–50ms;
- KV cache warmup planning for steady-state traffic (first 5–10 minutes of ramp are heavier).

If you use 3-bit quantization and enable prefix caching we can reduce this to 6 GPUs for the steady-state but still recommend 8 for headroom during peak spikes.

I'll add an appendix to the SOW with these numbers and an example cost projection.

— Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Exploring Dedicated — credits / bridge months / commit options

Jake — commercial thoughts from my side: we want the conversion to feel seamless for you. Proposed term structure: 

A) 12-month reserved commit priced at list less a conversion credit equivalent to 60% of the trailing 6 months of hosted spend (applied across months 1–4: 40%/30%/20%/10% phasing).
B) Two complementary bridge months where hosted invoicing continues and Dedicated reservation begins on month 3; credits applied to first two Dedicated invoices to avoid a billing step-up.
C) Option for a second-year renewal discount ladder tied to committed throughput utilization (>70% usage unlocks additional 7% off).

If Nimbus needs tighter cashflow, we can move to an 18-month commit with a slightly larger conversion credit but with smaller monthly reserved payments. I'm happy to model both.

— Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
